rules.observation: In configured boundary files, exported function parameters whose annotation names a configured trusted domain type are reported. This is a bounded ownership check, not a proof that every JSON value was decoded.
rules.rationale: External representations are not trusted domain values.
rules.title: Boundary parameters do not claim a trusted domain type

rules.observation: Reports explicit any syntax and compiler-reported implicit-any diagnostics in the selected scope.
rules.rationale: any erases TypeScript checking at the point it is used.
rules.title: any is forbidden

rules.observation: Reports as, type assertions, non-null assertions, @ts-ignore, and @ts-expect-error; policy chooses forbid or allow-with-receipt for each class.
rules.rationale: Assertions and suppression directives bypass or suppress checking.
rules.title: Soundness escape hatches are explicit policy evidence

rules.observation: Reports throw statements in configured domain files. It does not infer whether every function result is a result-like union.
rules.rationale: Expected domain failure should remain explicit data.
rules.title: Domain failures do not throw

rules.observation: For switch expressions whose checked union members expose a configured string-literal discriminator, reports missing literal cases. A default clause alone is not accepted as proof of handling.
rules.rationale: A new union case should not silently fall through.
rules.title: Configured discriminated unions are exhaustive

rules.observation: Reports non-literal element access in domain files unless it is lexically guarded by key in object or Object.hasOwn(object, key). It is not a proof of every runtime key invariant.
rules.rationale: Dynamic lookup can yield absent or unintended data.
rules.title: Dynamic indexed access is refined before use

rules.observation: Reports Array, Map, Set and mutable object properties in exported domain type/interface declarations. readonly is static only; no deep runtime immutability is claimed.
rules.rationale: Public mutable data permits callers to invalidate decisions after construction.
rules.title: Public domain contracts do not expose mutable collection or object shapes

rules.observation: Reports assignments through a property/index and recognized mutating collection methods in configured domain files.
rules.rationale: Mutation obscures value flow and invalidates referential reasoning.
rules.title: Domain mutation is forbidden

rules.observation: Reports imports of known Node infrastructure modules and direct use of fetch, console, process, timers, Math.random, and Date.now in domain files.
rules.rationale: Effects should be isolated at named boundaries.
rules.title: Domain modules do not directly use known infrastructure effects

rules.observation: Reports a domain import that resolves to a configured boundary/adapters source file. It does not infer architectural intent beyond that dependency edge.
rules.rationale: The core should receive capability inputs rather than concrete adapters.
rules.title: Domain modules do not depend on configured adapters

rules.observation: Reports references in domain files to a policy-listed transport/DTO type name. It does not prove runtime schema completeness.
rules.rationale: Transport representation requires an explicit decoding boundary.
rules.title: Configured transport type names do not enter domain code
